Hide GApps traces

Hide suspicious injections
Maps every file a module injects — files under each module’s system/ overlay and *.so under /data/adb/modules — so an inode/memory-map scan can’t spot them. Needs the SUS_MAP kernel feature.
Hide custom recovery paths
Hides leftover TWRP/OrangeFox/install-recovery traces (/data/recovery, install-recovery.sh, storage folders) when present.
Hide suspicious PTYs
Hides /dev/pts/0–5, the pseudo-terminals a root shell allocates. Off by default — can affect terminal apps.
Hide /system/addon.d
Hides the addon.d directory of survive-OTA scripts (e.g. 50-lineage.sh) that name a custom ROM.
Hide framework-res.apk
Maps framework-res.apk overlays under /system, a common resource-overlay detection point. Needs the SUS_MAP kernel feature.
Hide /data/local/tmp contents
Hides every entry under /data/local/tmp — the usual staging area for root tools and installers.
Hide non-standard storage folders
Hides top-level /storage/emulated/0 folders that aren’t standard media dirs (DCIM, Download, Android…). Broad — hides any stray folder you keep in storage root. Off by default.
Hide non-standard Android/ folders
Hides /storage/emulated/0/Android entries that aren’t data, media, or obb.
Hide LineageOS policy strings (advanced)
⚠ Risky. Redirects SELinux policy (sepolicy.cil, file_contexts) and lineage-mentioning .rc files to empty fakes. These are policy/init files — if something re-reads them at runtime you can hit SELinux denials or a service that won’t start. Leave off unless a check specifically needs it and you understand the risk. Needs the open_redirect kernel feature.
Hide vendor sepolicy strings
Hide compatibility_matrix strings
Hide sus mounts
Off
Always

Auto try_umount detected mounts
Skip kernel umount with ReZygisk/ZygiskNext
When ReZygisk or ZygiskNext is installed, let it handle unmounting instead of the kernel umount — they do their own, and doing both conflicts. Only takes effect when one of them is present; otherwise the module unmounts normally. On by default.
Disable SuSFS add_try_umount
Deprecated in SuSFS v2.0.0 — the add_try_umount backend was removed, so this has no effect on v2.0.0+ kernels (Nyx unmounts through KernelSU’s built-in kernel umount there). Only relevant on older kernels that still expose CONFIG_KSU_SUSFS_TRY_UMOUNT. Advanced — off by default.
Umount for zygote isolated services
Deprecated in SuSFS v2.0.0 — the command was removed, so this is a no-op on v2.0.0+ kernels (the built-in kernel umount covers isolated services). On older kernels it can break modules that overlay framework files; boot into rescue mode if you bootloop.

Credits
NyxSUSFS pairs a WebUI written from scratch with boot-stage logic that started from ksu_module_susfs, so it stays a drop-in for anyone already using that module.
SuSFS by simonpunk is the kernel magic that makes all of this possible. None of this exists without it.
ksu_module_susfs by sidex15 is the original module Nyx grew out of. Nyx keeps its config layout so it stays a friendly drop-in for anyone already using it, and ships sidex15's ksu_susfs binaries. Huge thanks for the foundation.
A number of Nyx's mount-hiding ideas were sparked by studying BRENE by rrr333nnn333. The ideas were reimplemented in Nyx's own way, but the inspiration deserves a shout-out.
The Zygisk-aware unmounting and mount-source detection were guided by the ReZygisk project (PerformanC), thanks for the pointers on doing it right.
Everything else, the WebUI, the targeted hiding, the glue, I built myself, with love for the community. Issues and translations welcome. Prop spoofing is a separate module, NyxProps.

Credits
NyxSUSFS pairs a WebUI written from scratch with boot-stage logic that started from ksu_module_susfs, so it stays a drop-in for anyone already using that module.
SuSFS by simonpunk is the kernel magic that makes all of this possible. None of this exists without it.
ksu_module_susfs by sidex15 is the original module Nyx grew out of. Nyx keeps its config layout so it stays a friendly drop-in for anyone already using it, and ships sidex15's ksu_susfs binaries. Huge thanks for the foundation.
A number of Nyx's mount-hiding ideas were sparked by studying BRENE by rrr333nnn333. The ideas were reimplemented in Nyx's own way, but the inspiration deserves a shout-out.
The Zygisk-aware unmounting and mount-source detection were guided by the ReZygisk project (PerformanC), thanks for the pointers on doing it right.
Everything else, the WebUI, the targeted hiding, the glue, I built myself, with love for the community. Issues and translations welcome. Prop spoofing is a separate module, NyxProps.

Hide custom-ROM traces
Searches /system, /vendor, /system_ext, /product and top-level /data for custom-ROM name strings and hides matches (sus_map + sus_path_loop). Higher = fewer file-type exclusions. Extreme also scans /data dalvik-cache, resource-cache and misc — thorough but slow, and hides more, so use only if a check still detects the ROM.

Hide ReVanced YouTube/Music
Hide loop/jbd2 mount info
Hide suspicious injections
Maps every file a module injects — files under each module’s system/ overlay and *.so under /data/adb/modules — so an inode/memory-map scan can’t spot them. Needs the SUS_MAP kernel feature.
Hide custom recovery paths
Hides leftover TWRP/OrangeFox/install-recovery traces (/data/recovery, install-recovery.sh, storage folders) when present.
Hide suspicious PTYs
Hides /dev/pts/0–5, the pseudo-terminals a root shell allocates. Off by default — can affect terminal apps.
Hide /system/addon.d
Hides the addon.d directory of survive-OTA scripts (e.g. 50-lineage.sh) that name a custom ROM.
Hide framework-res.apk
Maps framework-res.apk overlays under /system, a common resource-overlay detection point. Needs the SUS_MAP kernel feature.
Hide /data/local/tmp contents
Hides every entry under /data/local/tmp — the usual staging area for root tools and installers.
Hide non-standard storage folders
Hides top-level /storage/emulated/0 folders that aren’t standard media dirs (DCIM, Download, Android…). Broad — hides any stray folder you keep in storage root. Off by default.
Hide non-standard Android/ folders
Hides /storage/emulated/0/Android entries that aren’t data, media, or obb.
Hide LineageOS policy strings (advanced)
⚠ Risky. Redirects SELinux policy (sepolicy.cil, file_contexts) and lineage-mentioning .rc files to empty fakes. These are policy/init files — if something re-reads them at runtime you can hit SELinux denials or a service that won’t start. Leave off unless a check specifically needs it and you understand the risk. Needs the open_redirect kernel feature.
